newsitem.title: USA: INSTANT VIEW - US stocks seen up after Q3 ECI.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - US stocks seen up after Q3 ECI.

text.p: U.S. stocks are seen higher as the third-quarter Employee Cost Index came in a bit lower than expected and boost bonds, analysts said. The following are their comments:
PHILIP ORLANDO, CHIEF INVESTMENT OFFICER AT VALUE LINE ASSET MANAGEMENT:
-- "It's lower than expected. Bonds should rally on this. We dodged one economic bullet."
-- "I think stocks will trade a little bit higher at the open but there will be trepidation going into the balance of the week with more economic indicators."
-- Orlando did not see much cause for concern with October consumer confidence due out at 1000 EST/1500 GMT. "That will be a good number."
LARRY WACHTEL, MARKET ANALYST AT PRUDENTIAL SECURITIES:

-- "The (ECI) index was weaker than expected and the bonds are rallying. But the market is obviously tired and needs consolidation. The entire framework of caution will not be superceded by one number."

The long bond surged 18/32 to yield 6.79 percent. December S&P 500 index futures rose 1.65 to 702.00, indicated the Dow industrials might open about 14 points higher. The blue chip index shed 34 points in a rollercoaster session on Monday.
PETER CARDILLO, DIRECTOR OF RESEARCH AT WESTFALIA INVESTMENTS:

-- "The bond market has rallied and that is good news because it alleviates fears of inflation. But the stock market is not being driven by inflation fears at this time. The scare is the upcoming elections and the question of whether the Republicans manage to keep Congress."

-- "I suspect that we will have a higher opening and a repeat of yesterday when we had selling in the afternoon. I think the market is getting very close to an intermediary correction low. At worse there are another 30 to 40 points on the downside for the Dow and then we bounce."
